quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #21
										  					
  

36 Questions • Passing Score 30

questions.question: A driver license is a:

options.text: Requirement.
Privilege.
Right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Privilege.
questions.explanation: Driving is a privilege, not a right. All drivers must help keep roads safe. If you abuse this privilege, it can be taken away.

questions.question: You must always stop at which traffic lights?

options.text: Solid red lights, flashing red lights, and lights that are not working.
Solid red lights, red arrows, and flashing yellow lights.
Solid red lights, flashing red lights, and yellow lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Solid red lights, flashing red lights, and lights that are not working.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a solid red light, a flashing red light, or a light that is not working. A solid yellow light means the light will turn red soon—stop if you can do so safely. A flashing yellow light means slow down but you do not have to stop.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Slow down or stop.
Stop if necessary.
You must come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: An octagonal sign always means stop. Come to a complete stop at the stop line. If there is no stop line, stop before the crosswalk. If there is no crosswalk, stop before the intersection where you can see oncoming traffic.

questions.question: A police officer tells you to go through a red light. What should you do?

options.text: Stop until the light turns green.
Go through the intersection without stopping.
Come to a complete stop before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go through the intersection without stopping.
questions.explanation: Police officer directions always override traffic lights and signs. Follow the officer's directions.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: The same thing as a yield sign.
The light is about to turn green.
The same thing as a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same thing as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and go when it is safe. This is the same as a stop sign.

questions.question: When should your wheels NOT be pointed straight ahead?

options.text: When waiting to make a left turn at a traffic light.
When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.
When parked on the side of a level road with no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.
questions.explanation: While waiting to turn left, keep wheels straight so if hit from behind you won't swerve into oncoming traffic. On hills, turn wheels so the vehicle won't roll into traffic if brakes fail.

questions.question: When should you NOT use your horn?

options.text: When visibility ahead is limited.
If you might hit another vehicle.
Near blind pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near blind pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Do not use your horn near a blind pedestrian. It may be dangerous. Yield to the pedestrian and go when it is safe.

questions.question: What is the speed limit in any alley?

options.text: 20 mph.
15 mph.
25 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: 15 mph.
questions.explanation: The speed limit in any alley is always 15 mph, whether or not it is posted.

questions.question: You and the driver on your left reach a four-way stop at the same time. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on your left has the right-of-way.
You have the right-of-way.
Whoever is signaling to make a turn has the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at the same time to a four-way stop, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: You park facing uphill with no curb. Set the parking brake and:

options.text: Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.
Turn your wheels away from the edge of the road.
Keep your wheels facing straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill with no curb, turn your front wheels toward the edge of the road. This ensures the vehicle will roll off the road if brakes fail.

questions.question: If a tire blows out while driving, you should:

options.text: Apply the brake and hold it.
Hold the steering wheel tightly and use the brakes lightly.
Pull over quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel tightly and use the brakes lightly.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, hold the steering wheel tightly and keep the car straight. Slow down gradually by taking your foot off the gas and using light braking. Pull off the road safely when possible.

questions.question: How do you make room for cars entering the freeway?

options.text: Slow down.
Move to a different lane.
Keep your speed and position the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a different lane.
questions.explanation: Make room for vehicles entering the freeway. If possible, move to the next lane to create a gap. If you cannot move, adjust your speed to help them enter safely.

questions.question: Driving slower than other traffic is:

options.text: Good if the weather is bad.
Okay if you don't know the speed limit.
Often dangerous because other drivers may try unsafe passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often dangerous because other drivers may try unsafe passes.
questions.explanation: Driving slower than other traffic is dangerous. Drivers behind you may become impatient and take unsafe risks to pass you.

questions.question: When leaving the interstate, when should you reduce your speed?

options.text: About halfway through the deceleration lane.
As you approach the deceleration lane.
Immediately upon entering the deceleration lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Immediately upon entering the deceleration lane.
questions.explanation: Keep your speed on the interstate until you enter the deceleration lane. Then slow down to the speed posted for the exit ramp.

questions.question: Allow extra space when following a:

options.text: Station wagon.
Passenger vehicle.
Motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Allow extra space behind motorcycles. They can stop faster than other vehicles. You need room to stop if they brake suddenly. Motorcycles are also hard to see at night.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: No right turn.
Drive only in the direction of the arrow.
Curve ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive only in the direction of the arrow.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers to drive in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.question: Three important times to check for traffic behind you are before:

options.text: Backing, making a sharp turn, or crossing an intersection.
Backing, changing lanes, or slowing down quickly.
Changing lanes, crossing intersections, or slowing down quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Backing, changing lanes, or slowing down quickly.
questions.explanation: Check behind you before backing, changing lanes, slowing down, or driving down a long or steep hill.

questions.question: You consent to a chemical test for alcohol in your blood, breath, or urine:

options.text: Only if you have been drinking.
Whenever you drive in California.
Only if you have a collision.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whenever you drive in California.
questions.explanation: By driving in California, you agree to a breath, blood, or urine test if you are arrested for suspicion of driving under the influence.

questions.question: You are parking downhill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: When parking downhill, turn your wheels toward the edge of the road. Your car will roll away from traffic if the brakes fail. When parking uphill with a curb, turn toward the center instead so the car rolls into the curb.

questions.question: In a business district, when are U-turns legal?

options.text: Never, because they are dangerous.
Whenever oncoming vehicles are not a hazard.
At intersections, unless a sign says no U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections, unless a sign says no U-turn.
questions.explanation: In a business district, you may make a U-turn only at an intersection, unless a sign prohibits it. Some intersections have openings made for turns.

questions.question: A car is tailgating you on a two-lane road. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down gradually so the tailgater will pass you.
Speed up to increase the distance between cars.
Tap your brakes, then go back to normal speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually so the tailgater will pass you.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, change lanes if possible. If you cannot change lanes, slowly reduce your speed. This will encourage the tailgater to drive around you.

questions.question: The light is green, but traffic is blocking the intersection ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Turn left to find another route.
Wait outside the intersection until traffic clears.
Follow other vehicles and enter the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait outside the intersection until traffic clears.
questions.explanation: Do not enter the intersection if traffic is blocking it, even if your light is green. If you get stuck in the intersection when the light turns red, you will block cross traffic. You can get a ticket for blocking an intersection.

questions.question: When parallel parking facing downhill, how should you turn your wheels?

options.text: Turn them sharply toward the side of the road.
Turn them away from the side of the road.
Keep them straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn them sharply toward the side of the road.
questions.explanation: When parking downhill, turn your wheels toward the curb or edge of the road. When parking uphill without a curb, turn toward the edge. When parking uphill with a curb, turn away from the curb.

questions.question: When can you turn left on a red light?

options.text: From a one-way street onto a two-way street.
From a one-way street onto a one-way street.
From a two-way street onto a one-way street.

questions.correctAnswerText: From a one-way street onto a one-way street.
questions.explanation: You may turn left against a red light only when turning from a one-way street onto a one-way street. Check that no sign prohibits it. Yield to other vehicles, pedestrians, and bicyclists. Look both ways before turning.

questions.question: You want to pass a bicyclist in a narrow lane, but a car is coming toward you. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn and pass the bicyclist.
Slow down and let the car pass before you pass the bicyclist.
Wait for the bicyclist to leave the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the car pass before you pass the bicyclist.
questions.explanation: Handle one problem at a time. Let the oncoming car pass first. Then pass the bicyclist when it is safe.

questions.question: Oncoming headlights are blinding you at night. What should you do?

options.text: Look toward the right edge of the road.
Switch to high beam headlights.
Flash your lights on and off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If oncoming headlights are blinding you, glance toward the right edge of the road instead of looking ahead. This keeps your vehicle safe on the road until you pass the other car.

questions.question: Another driver is passing you in a no-passing zone. What should you do?

options.text: Pull off the road.
Keep the same speed and position.
Slow down so the other driver can safely return to the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down so the other driver can safely return to the lane.
questions.explanation: Slow down and let the passing vehicle return to the lane safely. This helps both drivers avoid hazards ahead.

questions.question: When driving on a multilane street with two-way traffic, where should you drive?

options.text: Next to other vehicles so they can see you.
Ahead of or behind other vehicles.
In the lane next to the centerline.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ahead of or behind other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Do not drive directly alongside another vehicle. The other driver might crowd your lane or change lanes without looking. Drive ahead of or behind vehicles instead.

questions.question: When entering a freeway, how should you check for traffic?

options.text: Use your rearview and side mirrors.
Use your rearview mirror only.
Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder to see traffic and avoid blind spots when entering a freeway.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you never do?

options.text: Cross the centerline in an intersection.
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.
Check for drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross the centerline in an intersection.
questions.explanation: Never change lanes in an intersection. Before changing lanes, check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder. Also look for drivers trying to enter the same lane.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with siren and flashing lights is approaching. What should you do?

options.text: Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.
Move to the right lane and drive slowly.
Stop immediately, even in an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Yield the right-of-way to emergency vehicles using sirens and flashing lights. Drive to the right edge of the road and stop. Avoid stopping in an intersection. You can move again after the vehicle passes.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must turn right.
All traffic must go straight.
A side road is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A side road is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that a side road will intersect ahead. Be alert and ready.

questions.question: When driving at night on a dimly lit street, what should you do?

options.text: Drive slow enough to stop within your headlights' range.
Use high beam headlights to see vehicles ahead.
Keep instrument panel lights bright so others see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slow enough to stop within your headlights' range.
questions.explanation: Drive more slowly at night because you cannot see as far ahead. Make sure you can stop within the area lit by your headlights.

questions.question: On a green arrow, what must you do?

options.text: Yield to vehicles, bicycles, and pedestrians in the intersection.
Yield to pedestrians only.
Wait four seconds before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to vehicles, bicycles, and pedestrians in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means go. Turn in the direction the arrow points after you yield to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians still in the intersection.

questions.question: When should you flash your brake lights or turn on your emergency flashers?

options.text: When you need to warn drivers of a crash ahead.
When you are parked in a traffic lane to make a delivery.
When you are backing out of a parking space.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you need to warn drivers of a crash ahead.
questions.explanation: If you see a crash ahead, warn drivers behind you by turning on your emergency flashers or by tapping your brake pedal three or four times quickly.

questions.question: You are getting ready to make a right turn. What should you do?

options.text: Signal and turn immediately.
Stop and let all other traffic go first.
Slow down or stop if needed, then turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down or stop if needed, then turn.
questions.explanation: When making a right turn, signal about 100 feet before the turn. Reduce your speed and stop behind the limit line if needed. Then make the turn.
